entries.label: A beautiful object used without fear
entries.description: She wants to become comfortable using an object she values rather than preserving it untouched.
expressionExamples: She might explain that she wants to become comfortable using an object she values rather than preserving it untouched.
Clarify what use the object was intended for.
entries.usageNotes: A self-directed candidate goal. Steps and outcomes require actual choices and supported play; they do not grant work, objects, skills, relationships or time passage.
entries.personalMotivation: She values a relationship with things that includes ordinary wear.
possibleFirstSteps: Clarify what use the object was intended for.
Distinguish reasonable care from avoidance.
possibleComplications: The object may genuinely be unsuitable for the intended use.
Its ownership or condition may be uncertain.
satisfyingOutcomes: If use is appropriate and hers to choose, she might enjoy it; otherwise, she could choose a suitable alternative without guilt.

entries.label: A quiet performance
entries.description: She wants to offer a short piece whose scale suits her rather than an imagined audience's demands.
expressionExamples: She might explain that she wants to offer a short piece whose scale suits her rather than an imagined audience's demands.
Choose a modest piece or excerpt.
entries.usageNotes: A self-directed candidate goal. Steps and outcomes require actual choices and supported play; they do not grant work, objects, skills, relationships or time passage.
entries.personalMotivation: She wants expression with control over its setting.
possibleFirstSteps: Choose a modest piece or excerpt.
Ask whether a small audience would welcome it.
possibleComplications: She may decide privacy matters more.
Listeners may ask for more than she wants to offer.
satisfyingOutcomes: If she chooses to perform, the agreed piece might be enough; declining or keeping it private can also complete the decision.

entries.label: A material contrast study
entries.description: She wants to compare tactile materials without treating one as inherently more refined.
expressionExamples: She might explain that she wants to compare tactile materials without treating one as inherently more refined.
Choose two suitable, permitted sample types.
entries.usageNotes: A self-directed candidate goal. Steps and outcomes require actual choices and supported play; they do not grant work, objects, skills, relationships or time passage.
entries.personalMotivation: She enjoys noticing how different surfaces serve different purposes.
possibleFirstSteps: Choose two suitable, permitted sample types.
Define one visual or practical comparison question.
possibleComplications: Available samples may differ in more than material.
Her favourite appearance may not suit the intended use.
satisfyingOutcomes: If the comparison is useful, she might record contextual preferences rather than rank materials universally.

entries.label: A reversible personal accent
entries.description: She wants to explore identity through a removable accessory rather than a permanent change.
expressionExamples: She might explain that she wants to explore identity through a removable accessory rather than a permanent change.
Choose an accent she actually likes.
entries.usageNotes: A self-directed candidate goal. Steps and outcomes require actual choices and supported play; they do not grant work, objects, skills, relationships or time passage.
entries.personalMotivation: She values experimentation she can freely revise.
possibleFirstSteps: Choose an accent she actually likes.
Check fit against established anatomy and clothing.
possibleComplications: The accessory may obscure a signature feature.
Its fastening may be unsuitable for her surface or joints.
satisfyingOutcomes: If a comfortable design is approved, she might choose to wear it on an occasion; no bodily modification is implied.

entries.label: A respectful portrait brief
entries.description: She wants a visual description that preserves her face, adult form and chosen emphasis.
expressionExamples: She wants a visual description that preserves her face, adult form and chosen emphasis.
Identify the approved appearance bundle.
entries.usageNotes: A self-directed candidate goal. Steps and outcomes require actual choices and supported play; they do not grant work, objects, skills, relationships or time passage.
entries.personalMotivation: She wants to be recognizable without being reduced to ancestry or allure.
possibleFirstSteps: Identify the approved appearance bundle.
Separate physical facts from optional pose and clothing choices.
possibleComplications: A dramatic effect may obscure anatomy.
A visual impression may be mistaken for personality or consent.
satisfyingOutcomes: If the brief survives review, it could guide a candidate portrait without automatically replacing any existing image.

entries.label: A collection allowed to end
entries.description: She wants to decide what a once-absorbing collection should become when her interest changes.
expressionExamples: She might explain that she wants to decide what a once-absorbing collection should become when her interest changes.
Identify what still matters to her.
entries.usageNotes: A self-directed candidate goal. Steps and outcomes require actual choices and supported play; they do not grant work, objects, skills, relationships or time passage.
entries.personalMotivation: She values continuity without being governed by old enthusiasm.
possibleFirstSteps: Identify what still matters to her.
Separate private or borrowed items from things she may freely release.
possibleComplications: Nostalgia may blur the collection's current purpose.
A proposed recipient may not want the surplus.
satisfyingOutcomes: If she chooses, she might keep a smaller selection or close the project; all transfers remain separate agreed events.

entries.label: A shared story with separate voices
entries.description: She wants to make a collaborative story without flattening the contributors into one tone.
expressionExamples: She might explain that she wants to make a collaborative story without flattening the contributors into one tone.
Agree on a modest fictional premise.
entries.usageNotes: A self-directed candidate goal. Steps and outcomes require actual choices and supported play; they do not grant work, objects, skills, relationships or time passage.
entries.personalMotivation: She values company that preserves authorship.
possibleFirstSteps: Agree on a modest fictional premise.
Ask each willing contributor what part they want to shape.
possibleComplications: Ideas may point toward different endings.
One contributor may want to withdraw.
satisfyingOutcomes: If everyone agrees, they might keep parallel versions or a clearly attributed collaboration rather than force uniformity.

entries.label: A listening library
entries.description: She wants a small set of music notes organized around how pieces invite listening rather than prestige.
expressionExamples: She wants a small set of music notes organized around how pieces invite listening rather than prestige.
Choose a narrow personal listening question.
entries.usageNotes: A self-directed candidate goal. Steps and outcomes require actual choices and supported play; they do not grant work, objects, skills, relationships or time passage.
entries.personalMotivation: She values attentive enjoyment.
possibleFirstSteps: Choose a narrow personal listening question.
Record only pieces and performances actually established.
possibleComplications: Descriptions may imply emotions every listener does not share.
She may want to keep some notes private.
satisfyingOutcomes: If the notes remain useful, she might create a modest personal guide with room for different responses.

entries.label: A goal she can reshape
entries.description: She wants to revisit a project whose original aim no longer interests her.
expressionExamples: She might explain that she wants to revisit a project whose original aim no longer interests her.
Name which part still matters.
entries.usageNotes: A self-directed candidate goal. Steps and outcomes require actual choices and supported play; they do not grant work, objects, skills, relationships or time passage.
entries.personalMotivation: She wants revision without humiliation.
possibleFirstSteps: Name which part still matters.
Distinguish genuine commitments from private expectations.
possibleComplications: She may worry that stopping disappoints someone.
Useful work already done may make the old goal feel compulsory.
satisfyingOutcomes: If obligations are honestly addressed, she might narrow, redirect or end the project without a failure narrative.

entries.label: A celebration chosen by its subject
entries.description: She wants a way to acknowledge a milestone without deciding another person's preferred celebration for them.
expressionExamples: She wants a way to acknowledge a milestone without deciding another person's preferred celebration for them.
Confirm that the milestone actually occurred.
entries.usageNotes: A self-directed candidate goal. Steps and outcomes require actual choices and supported play; they do not grant work, objects, skills, relationships or time passage.
entries.personalMotivation: She values affection that listens.
possibleFirstSteps: Confirm that the milestone actually occurred.
Ask whether and how its subject wants it acknowledged.
possibleComplications: The person may prefer privacy.
A group may have incompatible ideas about scale.
satisfyingOutcomes: If the subject welcomes it, a modest agreed acknowledgement might follow; choosing no celebration remains equally respectful.
